headline: Morgan Stanley says Nvidia and Broadcom are relatively shielded from the US shortage of electricity for data centres, but makers of memory chips and other parts could be hit.
score_reason: Pool score 5 kept: one brokerage's view of how the power shortage spreads through the chip supply chain, reported by Reuters.
importance_line: Shareholders in makers of memory and other chip parts could be hit first if power shortages delay AI data centres, while Nvidia and Broadcom are seen as safer, but this is one brokerage's estimate, not a reported cut in orders.
summary: Reuters reports that Morgan Stanley said on Monday that Nvidia and Broadcom are relatively insulated from a worsening US data-centre power shortage, because it does not see the bottlenecks putting their 2027 forecasts at risk. It warns that if chips cannot be put to use, customers could delay deliveries or cancel orders, with makers of memory, optical, power-management and analog parts most at risk, after the brokerage estimated last month that US data-centre builders face a 34% shortfall in the power they need through 2028, even after counting on-site generation and fuel cells.
